newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai firm says Kazakhstan, N.Korea dumping steel.
newsitem.headline: Thai firm says Kazakhstan, N.Korea dumping steel.

text.p: Thailand's Sahaviriya Steel Industries, hard-hit by cheap steel imports in 1996, said on Monday it had launched complaints against steel dumping by Kazakhstan and North Korea.
SSI president, Adisak Lowjun, told reporters the company had filed the complaints with the Commerce Ministry after compiling information about the alleged dumping.
But a senior commerce ministry official refused to say if the ministry planned to investigate the dumping charge.

"Normally, we don't reveal whether we plan to investigate a charge or not. We have to look carefully at the information provided by the complainant to see if it warrants an investigation," said Thawatchai Sophastienphong, deputy head of the department of business economics.
"If it does, we will formally announce it," he said.

The industry last year lodged similar complaints against steel imports from Russia, Ukraine and Poland, leading to the imposition of anti-dumping duties of about 25 to 52 percent on hot-rolled steel and structural steel from those countries.
SSI's Adisak said he was confident of his firm's findings.
"We must be sure of our data and information before we can submit it to the authorities," he said.
He earlier estimated that steel imports from Kazakhstan amounted to 50,000-100,000 tonnes a year at around $260-270 per tonne while SSI's product was sold at around $340 per tonne.
Thailand imported 1.4-1.5 million tonnes of steel in 1996. According to Adisak, almost 80 percent of that amount came from countries that dumped on market.
